hypothesis: Replacing exact 32-byte completed trigger continuations with decoder-rebuilt three-byte receipt references saves at least 525 LZMA payload bytes on opening 250K versus the identical raw LZMA backend.
interfaces_exposed: raw bytes -> causal trigger receipt IR with paid copy opcodes -> identical LZMA backend -> exact inverse
kill_condition: Retire this fixed 32-byte explicit-copy representation if neither receipt IR saves 525 LZMA payload bytes at opening 250K, if source exceeds 12,000 bytes, or if any inverse or determinism check fails; do not sweep copy length, history size, keys, opcodes, or LZMA settings.
promotion_condition: At opening 250K, either C0 or E0 receipt IR must beat raw LZMA payload by at least 525 bytes; every IR and selected archive must roundtrip and the selected archive must re-encode byte-identically.
rejection_reason: Exact opening-250K receipt IR failed the frozen mature-backend gate: C0 and E0 reduced raw IR by 6,612 and 11,832 bytes but increased identical LZMA payload by 260 and 304 bytes. RAW was selected; all inverses and determinism checks passed.
retired_neighborhoods: The raw order-1 TESBE predictor proves trigger alignment only; this proposal tests a paid reversible representation against a mature identical backend.
title: Paid trigger-receipt copy IR over LZMA
